case_vignette: A 26-year-old woman attends ED for the fourth time in 18 months with severe dysmenorrhoea, pelvic pain and near-syncope on standing, previously discharged as IBS, anxiety and vasovagal episodes. Today she is tachycardic upright with a normal ECG and a prior normal pelvic ultrasound, and the decision point bites: reassure and discharge again, refer down the NICE laparoscopy-or-nothing gynaecology queue, or do a 10-minute active stand test and document the pathway the guidelines disagree on.
rationale: What is new is going back to Nnoaham itself instead of the meme number, recovering the buried state-vs-private gap and testing it against Hadfield, NICE versus ESHRE thresholds, and POTS as a parallel system output; these six sources carry the anchor, the bias lesson, the UK pathway, and the POTS mirror, and deep-dive fits because the three mechanisms — test uninvented, unfunded, or orphaned without referral — need untangling, not a two-sided fight.

sources.title: Nnoaham et al. 2011: endometriosis impact across ten countries (Fertil Steril)
sources.why: Anchor source: 1,418 women, 6.7-year mean delay, plus the rarely-cited 8.3y state-funded vs 5.5y private gap that reframes delay as system design.

sources.title: Hadfield et al. 1996: delay in endometriosis diagnosis, USA and UK survey
sources.why: Historical control showing 11.7y US / 8.0y UK delays from self-help-group recruits — why selection bias inflates the numbers we still quote.

sources.title: NICE NG73: Endometriosis — diagnosis and management (2017, updated 2024)
sources.why: UK commissioning anchor: laparoscopy-with-histology threshold decides who queues, where, and how long.

sources.title: ESHRE guideline: endometriosis (Becker et al., Human Reproduction Open, 2022)
sources.why: Counterpoint to NICE: imaging/clinical diagnosis without diagnostic-only laparoscopy — same disease, lower test threshold, shorter pathway.

sources.title: 2015 HRS expert consensus on POTS, IST and vasovagal syncope (Sheldon et al.)
sources.why: Proof diagnoses can postdate patients by decades: formal POTS criteria only from 2015, explaining years of anxiety mislabels.

sources.title: Tiotsop et al. 2026: POTS diagnostic strategies, test accuracy, misdiagnosis
sources.why: Both sides in one paper: 24-month median delay with 75% prior misdiagnosis, plus tachycardia-mimic data that keeps the overdiagnosis warning honest.

title: Six Years Is The Average, Not The Outlier — Diagnostic Delay — 2026-09-17
